questions.question: What is the key three-component intermediate formed during the Strecker synthesis of alanine from acetaldehyde?

options.label: A
options.text: A β-amino acid ester.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic diketopiperazine.

options.label: C
options.text: An α-aminonitrile [CH₃CH(NH₂)CN] formed by addition of cyanide to the in situ generated imine, which is subsequently hydrolyzed in acid to alanine.

options.label: D
options.text: An α-hydroxy acid chloride.

questions.correct_answer: An α-aminonitrile [CH₃CH(NH₂)CN] formed by addition of cyanide to the in situ generated imine, which is subsequently hydrolyzed in acid to alanine.
questions.explanation: Acetaldehyde condenses with ammonia to form an imine; cyanide adds nucleophilically to form the α-aminonitrile intermediate.

questions.topic: HVZ Reaction Enol Acyl Bromide Intermediate
questions.question: What is the reactive enol intermediate during the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) α-bromination of carboxylic acids by Br₂/PBr₃?

options.label: A
options.text: A cyclic bromonium ion on the carbonyl oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: The enol form of the acyl bromide [R-CH=C(OH)Br], which is far more nucleophilic toward Br₂ than the enol of the parent carboxylic acid.

options.label: C
options.text: A carboxylate radical anion.

options.label: D
options.text: A carbocation formed by loss of carbon dioxide.

questions.correct_answer: The enol form of the acyl bromide [R-CH=C(OH)Br], which is far more nucleophilic toward Br₂ than the enol of the parent carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: PBr₃ converts the acid to an acyl bromide; its enol undergoes rapid α-bromination followed by exchange with unreacted acid to regenerate acyl bromide.

questions.question: In the diethyl acetamidomalonate synthesis of amino acids, why is the α-proton exceptionally acidic (pKa ~ 13)?

options.label: A
options.text: The α-carbon is an aromatic radical.

options.label: B
options.text: The α-carbon is sp hybridized.

options.label: C
options.text: The α-hydrogen is flanked by three electron-withdrawing groups (two esters and one acetamide), providing massive resonance stabilization to the resulting enolate carbanion.

options.label: D
options.text: The acetamido group contains a positively charged nitrogen.

questions.correct_answer: The α-hydrogen is flanked by three electron-withdrawing groups (two esters and one acetamide), providing massive resonance stabilization to the resulting enolate carbanion.
questions.explanation: Flanking ester and amide carbonyls delocalize the negative charge across multiple electronegative oxygens, making deprotonation by NaOEt facile.

questions.question: What defines the isoelectric point (pI) of an amino acid mechanistically?

options.label: A
options.text: The pH at which all peptide bonds hydrolyze spontaneously.

options.label: B
options.text: The pH at which the amino acid boils.

options.label: C
options.text: The precise pH at which the concentration of the dipolar zwitterionic form with net charge zero is maximized ([NH₃⁺-CHR-COO⁻]), exactly balancing positive and negative forms.

options.label: D
options.text: The pH at which the amino acid becomes insoluble in water.

questions.correct_answer: The precise pH at which the concentration of the dipolar zwitterionic form with net charge zero is maximized ([NH₃⁺-CHR-COO⁻]), exactly balancing positive and negative forms.
questions.explanation: At the isoelectric point pI = (pKa₁ + pKa₂)/2, the amino acid carries no net electrical charge and does not migrate in an electric field.

questions.question: What is the sequential mechanism by which phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC) cleaves the N-terminal residue of a peptide?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-terminal carboxyl group.

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidation of the N-terminal residue by permanganate.

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the N-terminal amine on PITC (pH 9) to form a phenylthiocarbamoyl peptide → anhydrous acid cleavage to a cyclic thiazolinone → rearrangement to stable PTH-amino acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Complete hydrolysis of all peptide bonds simultaneously in 6 M HCl.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the N-terminal amine on PITC (pH 9) to form a phenylthiocarbamoyl peptide → anhydrous acid cleavage to a cyclic thiazolinone → rearrangement to stable PTH-amino acid.
questions.explanation: Edman degradation selectively labels and cleaves only the N-terminal residue as a PTH derivative without hydrolyzing internal peptide bonds.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic classification of the reaction between 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene (DNFB) and the N-terminal amine of a peptide?

options.label: A
options.text: Diels-Alder cycloaddition.

options.label: B
options.text: Free radical substitution.

options.label: C
options.text: Electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS).

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (SNAr) where the amine attacks the fluorinated carbon, forming a Meisenheimer complex that expels fluoride to yield a yellow DNP-peptide.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (SNAr) where the amine attacks the fluorinated carbon, forming a Meisenheimer complex that expels fluoride to yield a yellow DNP-peptide.
questions.explanation: The ortho/para nitro groups activate the ring toward SNAr attack by the N-terminal amino nucleophile, yielding a labeled DNP derivative.

questions.topic: Boc Protecting Group Acid Cleavage Mechanism
questions.question: Why does trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) cleave tert-butoxycarbonyl (Boc) protecting groups under mild conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: TFA reduces the carbamate to an alkane.

options.label: B
options.text: TFA acts as a strong nucleophile that displaces the amine.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation of the carbamate carbonyl triggers loss of a stable tert-butyl carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺], which expels CO₂ gas and regenerates the free ammonium trifluoroacetate salt.

options.label: D
options.text: TFA oxidizes the tert-butyl group to acetone.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the carbamate carbonyl triggers loss of a stable tert-butyl carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺], which expels CO₂ gas and regenerates the free ammonium trifluoroacetate salt.
questions.explanation: The stability of the tert-butyl cation drives rapid fragmentation of the protonated carbamate with loss of CO₂ gas and isobutylene.

questions.question: What is the reactive electrophile formed when Boc-alanine reacts with DCC in peptide synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: An O-acylisourea intermediate, which converts the carboxyl oxygen into an exceptional leaving group that is rapidly attacked by the amino nucleophile to form the peptide bond.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic anhydride.

options.label: C
options.text: A free acylium cation in solution.

options.label: D
options.text: An insoluble DCU salt.

questions.correct_answer: An O-acylisourea intermediate, which converts the carboxyl oxygen into an exceptional leaving group that is rapidly attacked by the amino nucleophile to form the peptide bond.
questions.explanation: DCC activates the carboxylic acid into an O-acylisourea, enabling nucleophilic acyl substitution by the free amine at room temperature.

questions.question: How is the growing peptide chain anchored during Merrifield solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)?

options.label: A
options.text: The peptide is suspended in magnetic nanoparticles.

options.label: B
options.text: The C-terminal carboxylic acid is covalently attached via an ester or amide linkage to a chloromethylated polystyrene resin bead, allowing excess reagents to be washed away.

options.label: C
options.text: The peptide forms non-covalent hydrogen bonds with silica gel.

options.label: D
options.text: The peptide is encapsulated in liposomes.

questions.correct_answer: The C-terminal carboxylic acid is covalently attached via an ester or amide linkage to a chloromethylated polystyrene resin bead, allowing excess reagents to be washed away.
questions.explanation: Covalent attachment to insoluble resin beads enables rapid, automated filtration and washing after every coupling and deprotection cycle.

questions.question: What chemical transformation links two polypeptide chains covalently via their cysteine side chains?

options.label: A
options.text: Condensation of two carboxyl groups to an anhydride.

options.label: B
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of amine on an amide.

options.label: C
options.text: Mild oxidation of two nucleophilic thiol groups (-SH) to form a covalent disulfide bridge (-S-S-), which can be reversed by reducing agents like 2-mercaptoethanol.

options.label: D
options.text: E2 elimination to form a dehydroalanine double bond.

questions.correct_answer: Mild oxidation of two nucleophilic thiol groups (-SH) to form a covalent disulfide bridge (-S-S-), which can be reversed by reducing agents like 2-mercaptoethanol.
questions.explanation: Cysteine thiols readily undergo reversible two-electron oxidation to form covalent disulfide linkages essential for protein tertiary and quaternary structure.

questions.question: In the diethyl acetamidomalonate synthesis of amino acids, why is the α-proton exceptionally acidic (pKa ~ 13)?

options.label: A
options.text: The α-hydrogen is flanked by three electron-withdrawing groups (two esters and one acetamide), providing massive resonance stabilization to the resulting enolate carbanion.

options.label: B
options.text: The α-carbon is sp hybridized.

options.label: C
options.text: The α-carbon is an aromatic radical.

options.label: D
options.text: The acetamido group contains a positively charged nitrogen.

questions.correct_answer: The α-hydrogen is flanked by three electron-withdrawing groups (two esters and one acetamide), providing massive resonance stabilization to the resulting enolate carbanion.
questions.explanation: Flanking ester and amide carbonyls delocalize the negative charge across multiple electronegative oxygens, making deprotonation by NaOEt facile.

questions.question: What defines the isoelectric point (pI) of an amino acid mechanistically?

options.label: A
options.text: The pH at which all peptide bonds hydrolyze spontaneously.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: The precise pH at which the concentration of the dipolar zwitterionic form with net charge zero is maximized ([NH₃⁺-CHR-COO⁻]), exactly balancing positive and negative forms.

questions.correct_answer: The precise pH at which the concentration of the dipolar zwitterionic form with net charge zero is maximized ([NH₃⁺-CHR-COO⁻]), exactly balancing positive and negative forms.
questions.explanation: At the isoelectric point pI = (pKa₁ + pKa₂)/2, the amino acid carries no net electrical charge and does not migrate in an electric field.

questions.question: What is the sequential mechanism by which phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC) cleaves the N-terminal residue of a peptide?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete hydrolysis of all peptide bonds simultaneously in 6 M HCl.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-terminal carboxyl group.

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the N-terminal amine on PITC (pH 9) to form a phenylthiocarbamoyl peptide → anhydrous acid cleavage to a cyclic thiazolinone → rearrangement to stable PTH-amino acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation of the N-terminal residue by permanganate.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the N-terminal amine on PITC (pH 9) to form a phenylthiocarbamoyl peptide → anhydrous acid cleavage to a cyclic thiazolinone → rearrangement to stable PTH-amino acid.
questions.explanation: Edman degradation selectively labels and cleaves only the N-terminal residue as a PTH derivative without hydrolyzing internal peptide bonds.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic classification of the reaction between 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene (DNFB) and the N-terminal amine of a peptide?

questions.question: How is the growing peptide chain anchored during Merrifield solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)?

questions.explanation: Covalent attachment to insoluble resin beads enables rapid, automated filtration and washing after every coupling and deprotection cycle.
